name: Tome of Legends
oracle_text:
This artifact enters with a page counter on it.
Whenever your commander enters or attacks, put a page counter on this artifact.
{1}, {T}, Remove a page counter from this artifact: Draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Whenever your commander enters or attacks, put a page counter on this artifact.

needs.what: honour the `owner` key ("you" / "opponent") in a trigger `filter`, i.e. in triggers.matches_card_filter, compared against the subject object's GameObject.owner relative to the ability source's controller -- so "whenever your commander enters or attacks" is two triggers (permanent_enters, attacks) with controller "any" and filter {is_commander: true, owner: "you"}. The rest of the card is already expressible: a card-level replacements entry {event: self_enters_with_counters, counter: page, amount: 1} (Diamond City shape) and an activated ability with cost {mana: {1}, tap: true, remove_counters: {amount: 1, counter: page}} drawing one card.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: 903.3 makes "your commander" a matter of ownership. Norn's Choirmaster's shape (trigger controller "you" + filter is_commander) means "a commander you control": it misses your own commander while an opponent controls it and fires on an opponent's commander you have stolen -- selectors.py's own `owner` docstring calls that a genuinely different set now that gain_control exists. `owner` is in selector_keys and is read by selectors.matches and characteristics' static filter, but triggers.matches_card_filter never reads it, so writing it in a trigger filter would load and be silently ignored. The workaround of an intervening-if condition {exists: {binding: subject, is_commander: true, owner: you}} is also wrong: trigger conditions are re-checked on resolution (603.4), so removing the commander in response would cancel the page counter, which the printed card (no intervening if) does not allow.
